W2 (empirical), after E016. Best is E016: 6.580 s, 0.7607 (E015 recipe with weight decay halved). The margin over 0.753 is about 0.77 pp, though some of it is probably reshuffle noise.

Measured (3 seeds, all complete): E001 9ep eager 0.7430/9.43. E004 compiled 0.7486/9.04. E005 +EMA 0.7583/9.10. E006 +Muon 0.7649/9.45. E007 +prog-res 0.7590/7.33. E008 8.5ep 0.7572/6.98. E009 LR floor 0 0.7564/6.99. E010 width 512 0.7548/6.64. E011 aggressive res 0.7451/5.70. E012 rerun of E010: bit-identical accuracy, time within 0.1%. E013 LS 0.2: 0.7551. E014 Muon lr x1.5: 0.7557. E015 CUDA graphs: 0.7574/6.578. E016 wd/2: 0.7607/6.580.

Mechanisms:
1. Epoch dial: -0.5 epoch costs about 0.18 pp and saves about 4.8% time, roughly linear (E007 to E008).
2. Compile saves about 4% (E001 to E004).
3. EMA/Lookahead: +0.97 pp for +0.06 s, the cheapest gain (E005).
4. Muon: +0.66 pp for +0.35 s (E006).
5. Progressive resizing: -22% time for -0.59 pp. Time tracks pixel count (E007).
6. Width 576 to 512: -4.8% time for -0.25 pp, about the epoch-dial exchange rate (E010).
7. Resolution cliff: -14% time for -1.4 pp (E011).
8. Label smoothing, Muon lr and LR floor are flat within noise (E009, E013, E014). Weight decay /2 gave +0.3 pp (E016), which is marginal, and the direction may continue.
9. CUDA graphs: only -0.9% time, so the run is compute-bound (E015). The accuracy changes there and in E016 are partly reshuffle noise.
10. Noise: runs are deterministic per seed. Recipe-reshuffle noise on 3-seed means is about ±0.2 pp. Time noise is about 0.5%. Fixed costs are about 0.3-0.5 s.

Misses: I under-predicted EMA, Muon, resizing and E016 accuracy, and over-predicted E009 and E011. Lesson: accuracy-neutral knobs land within ±0.25 pp, and time stays put unless pixels or FLOPs change.

Unsure: how much of the 6.6 s is fixed cost versus per-step compute. Whether lower wd keeps helping. Whether plain EMA matches Lookahead. The held-out seed spread. Whether the 28 px phase is dispensable.

With about 0.77 pp of slack, the real lever is spending it on epochs or FLOPs: about 1.5 epochs, or a narrower group 2, saving about 8-12%.

forecasts.reason: Plain EMA that does not reset the fast weights probably recovers most of the gain, but BN-buffer EMA mismatch is a risk; time is unchanged.
Replacing 28 px steps with 32 px adds pixels and so time (about +4-5%), and adds accuracy of about 0.2-0.4 pp. It is a worse trade than the epoch dial.
Cutting 24 px epochs is cheap in time (-4%) and costs about 0.1-0.2 pp, so it stays above the bar.
The rerun is likely bit-identical; held-out seeds probably average a little below the 3-seed mean by 0.1-0.3 pp.
The optimizer knobs are flat within noise; momentum 0.8 is probably neutral or slightly worse with Muon.
Group 2 carries about half of the FLOPs, so 384 to 320 saves about 6% of time for about 0.2-0.3 pp, in line with the width exchange rate.

cruxes: Is the 0.7607 of E016 real margin, or reshuffle noise, as seen from the held-out-seed offset? This decides how many epochs or how much width can be cut.
Does the time gap between 24 and 32 px come from conv FLOPs, or from fixed costs (data, augmentation, interpolation)? This sets how much a narrower group 2 or fewer epochs can save.
Does Lookahead reset or plain EMA give the endpoint-averaging gain? This decides whether a cheaper averaging scheme is possible.
